title: Invariant normalized blowup dominating an orbit of blowups
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S_0$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme. Let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $S_0$ and $k$. Let $I\subset\mathcal O_{S_0}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal equal to $\mathcal O_{S_0}$ on a dense open $U_0$. Put $U=\bigcap_{h\in H}h(U_0)$, $J=\prod_{h\in H}h(I)$, $V=\operatorname{Bl}_I(S_0)$, $B=\operatorname{Bl}_J(S_0)$, and let $\nu:S=B^\nu\to B$ be normalization in the function field. Here $h(I)$ is the ideal transported by the automorphism $h$. The scheme $B$ is integral, its map to $S_0$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense, and it canonically dominates every $\operatorname{Bl}_{h(I)}(S_0)$. The map $\nu$ is finite and birational. The scheme $S$ is normal integral projective of finite type over $k$; $S\to S_0$ is H-projective and birational, identifies $k(S)=k(S_0)$, and is an isomorphism over $U$. There are compatible $H$-actions on $B$ and $S$ for which $S\to B\to S_0$ is equivariant. In particular $S$ has an $S_0$-morphism to $V$. The open $U$ is invariant and dense. Birational means an isomorphism between dense open subschemes.

All group actions are by automorphisms, may be nonfaithful, and commute with the displayed maps; they may act on the ground field. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target, independently of the name of the acting group. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Schematic closure is the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of restriction of functions to the specified subscheme.

Notions used: [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-sc-normalization], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Ideal sheaves and their products use [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Ideal sheaves and their products use [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers].

source.place: Tags 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); morphisms.tex Tags 035S (lemma-nagata-normalization), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective). Combine product-ideal common domination with the invariant Rees algebra and functorial normalization, as in de Jong (1997) §2.10.

proof.text: Every translate $h(U_0)$ is a dense open of the integral scheme $S_0$. Their finite intersection $U$ contains the generic point and is dense; $g(U)=\bigcap_h(gh)(U_0)=U$. By the affine-local definition of ideal products, $J$ is quasi-coherent: locally its generators are the finitely many products of generators of the finitely many factors. Thus it is of finite type. On $U$ every factor is the unit ideal, so $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and $J$ is nonzero. Transport preserves ideal multiplication, and reindexing $h\mapsto gh$ gives $g(J)=J$. No faithfulness or $k$-linearity is used.

source.place: Tags 02ND, 02NS: verification of the nonzero, quasi-coherent, finite-type ideal hypotheses

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-projective-geometry] to the nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $J$ on the integral scheme $S_0$. It gives that $B$ is integral and $b:B\to S_0$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], $b$ is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type, [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) shows that $B$ is of finite type over $k$.

Because $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$, the open $U$ lies in $S_0\setminus V(J)$. Restrict [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] further to $U$ to identify $b^{-1}(U)\to U$ with the identity. This is a nonempty open in the integral scheme $B$, hence dense. Thus $b$ is birational in the stated dense-open sense. Computing rational functions on this common dense open, using [def-sc-function-field], identifies $k(B)=k(S_0)$ canonically; call this field $K$.

Fix $h\in H$ and put $J_h=\prod_{g\ne h}g(I)$, taking the empty product to be the unit ideal. Then $J=h(I)J_h$. Extension of ideals along $b$ preserves this identity: locally both sides are generated by the same products of images of sections. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $J\mathcal O_B$ is an effective Cartier ideal. Apply [lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor] on $B$ to $(h(I)\mathcal O_B)(J_h\mathcal O_B)$: each factor is effective Cartier and hence invertible. The universal property [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] now gives the unique $S_0$-morphism $d_h:B\to\operatorname{Bl}_{h(I)}S_0$, using the canonical quotient $b^*h(I)\twoheadrightarrow h(I)\mathcal O_B$. This quotient is the image inside $\mathcal O_B$, so there is no choice of a line quotient. In particular $d_1$ maps to $V$.

source.place: Tag 0806 (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up), applied to each factor after principalization; current blueprint lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor

proof.text: For $h\in H$, regard $B$ as an $S_0$-scheme by $h\circ b$. Since $h(J)=J$, the extended ideal of $J$ for this map is again $J\mathcal O_B$, invertible by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] with the canonical image quotient to obtain a unique map $\beta_h:B\to B$ satisfying $b\beta_h=hb$. The composites $\beta_g\beta_h$ and $\beta_{gh}$ are maps over the same map $ghb$ and induce the same canonical quotient onto $J\mathcal O_B$; uniqueness gives $\beta_g\beta_h=\beta_{gh}$. Likewise $\beta_1=1$, so $\beta_{h^{-1}}$ is the inverse of $\beta_h$. These maps form the required action on $B$. Their compatibility with the original action on $k$ follows by composing $b\beta_h=hb$ with the structure map of $S_0$.

source.place: Tag 0806 (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up): uniqueness applied to automorphisms preserving the centre

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] with $V=B$, $H=k(B)=K$ (the letter $H$ in that node denotes a field), and the degree-one finite extension $M=K$. Its normalization is exactly $S=B^
u$ of [def-sc-normalization]. It is normal integral of finite type over $k$, and $
u$ is finite with $k(S)=K$. The theorem [lem-sc-normalization-exists] applied to the integral finite-type $k$-scheme $B$ gives birationality of $
u$. The open $b^{-1}(U)$ is normal because it is isomorphic to the open $U$ of the normal scheme $S_0$. Consequently [lem-sc-normalization-over-normal-locus] gives that $
u$ is an isomorphism over $b^{-1}(U)$. Thus $S	o S_0$ is an isomorphism over $U$, and both inverse images are nonempty dense opens of integral schemes. This proves the claimed birationality and identifies $k(S)=k(S_0)$.

Use the isomorphism-functoriality clause of [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] for the action $\beta_h$ on $B$ and the compatible left field action $A_h=(\beta_{h^{-1}})^*$ on $K=k(B)$. It supplies a unique semilinear lift to $S$, preserving identities and composition. Hence these lifts form an $H$-action and $\nu$ is equivariant. The preceding action on $B$ makes $b$ equivariant, so the composite is equivariant as well. Compatibility with the action on $k$ is included in that clause; no assumption that $h$ fixes $k$ or acts faithfully is needed. Finally $d_1\circ\nu:S\to V$ is an $S_0$-morphism because both $d_1$ and $
u$ are maps over $S_0$.

The given projective embedding $S_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ supplies an ample invertible sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] to $b$, which is projective in the projective-bundle sense by Step 2: thus $b$ is H-projective. Compose with the given H-projective structure map of $S_0$ using [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]; $B/k$ is H-projective. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible] again, now to this embedding of $B$, gives an ample invertible sheaf on $B$. Since $\nu$ is finite, [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle] makes it projective in the projective-bundle sense, and [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes it H-projective. Two further applications of [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] give that $S\to S_0$ and $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are H-projective. Together with Steps 1--7, this proves every assertion, with H-projective understood as the finite-projective-space convention, not an equivariant embedding condition.

Step 8: ample sheaf on S_0, then 087S for b, 01WE for B/k, ample sheaf on B, 0B3I plus 087S for ν, then compositions; hypotheses checked.
